mustKnow.item: Thesis: 'strategic investing' in miners = scale in step by step (better than DCA); buy technically strong but not-extended names first ('strength comes to strength', institutions buy trend); wait on extended leaders for shallow dips; wait on weak names for a correction, when they fall hardest; aim for a good blended portfolio entry
Context: gold rising, GDXJ likely broke its downtrend; gold correction is typical for a bull market; gold ~20% ($1,200) below ATH; a drop to 4,000 (~9.5%) is unlikely; stress scenario gold ~4,125
mustKnow.note: Ours has GDXJ and the 'normal correction' point but explicitly drops the 4,125 and 4,000 levels as 'ambiguous'.

mustKnow.item: Activity this week: bought 3 positions, 4th only 50% filled

BUY / accumulate now: SSR Mining (SSRM; uptrend, not super extended), New Pacific Metals (NUAG, silver; bounced off 50-day, ~20% to old highs), GoGold (GGD) and Artemis Gold (ARTG) named as the upside names he is buying
mustKnow.note: Ours has SSR as 'watch' (should be buy) and GGD/Artemis only in sentiment. LeapEdge has SSRM and New Pacific with a wrong ticker, and misses GGD/Artemis.

mustKnow.item: Bought: 1911 Gold (added at lower end of support, held 50-day; still below 200-day, long-term downtrend intact)
mustKnow.note: An actual purchase that LeapEdge omits.

mustKnow.item: Next Gold Mining (NexGold): owned; wanted to add but no pullback to the 50-day came; broke above the 200-day, bull flag, 'a lot of room to run'
mustKnow.note: LeapEdge has a keyPoint but no idea.

mustKnow.item: WAIT for shallow pullback (love, extended): Banyan Gold (not owned) and Cabral Gold (owned, ~C$500M cap, may be topping)
WAIT for correction (weak): McEwen Mining (below 50/200, downtrend) and Lundin Mining ('dud', likely to break support and see stop cascades in a sell-off)
Risks: broad market correction, dollar 'to the moon', gold pullback -> weak miners hit hardest
Teaser: a coming 'change in the mining industry' will alter the accumulation strategy (VIP video)

ours.text: k2: 'Gold mining stock selection focuses on technicals over fundamentals because gold has universal global demand...'
ours.problem: Wrong causality. He leaves fundamentals out because this video is 'purely strategic'. The global-demand point only says jurisdiction (made-in-US) doesn't matter for gold, unlike critical metals.

ours.text: SSR Mining 'in an uptrend above its 250-day moving average'
ours.problem: Repeats an ASR garble ('250-day' = '200, 50-day'). LeapEdge read it correctly.
Understated. It sits under 'The stocks that I will buy right now'; it is a buy.

ours.text: Omissions: drops 'gold down to 4,125' as ambiguous units, and Cabral '~500 Canadian' mcap
ours.problem: Over-cautious. Gold at 4,125 is an unambiguous gold-price scenario (the 'therapy session' is an ASR artifact). The omission note removes a key stress level.

ours.text: Lundin: one call 'watch' and one call 'avoid'; Banyan sentiment rows: neutral/avoid, bullish/watch, bullish/avoid
ours.problem: Contradictory duplicate stances for the same name.

ours.text: k8 and k9 are near-identical ('Recent corrections in the price of gold are typical...')

leapedge.problem: Wrong ticker. New Pacific Metals trades as NUAG (NYSE American/TSX).

leapedge.text: 'Ignore fundamentals for gold stocks, as gold is a global commodity with high liquidity regardless of the production location.'
leapedge.problem: Same causality error as ours, stated as a general rule. The creator never says to ignore fundamentals in general; he loves Cabral 'fundamentally'.
The video is about strategic long-term accumulation ('I believe in them long-term'). Only New Pacific is framed as a swing.

leapedge.text: Banyan idea stance 'long', counted in verdict '3 LONG'
leapedge.problem: Overstated. He is explicitly not buying and does not own it; this is a watch/wait-for-dip.
Mild overstatement. 'Even better', 'a lot of potential'; he does not say he bought it.

SSR Mining as a buy (labeled watch)

sentimentIssues: 26 rows for 12 names; Banyan x4 with three different stances, Cabral x3, Lundin x2 (neutral and bearish), gold x3.
SSR Mining is 'watch' in call and sentiment although it is in the buy-now bucket.
GGD/Artemis are 'watch' in one row and 'long' in another; they should be long (buying).
Rows for the spoken commodity 'gold' with ticker null add noise. Either map to XAU/GLD or drop them.
The GDXJ row appears twice (long and neutral).
why: Ours maps the creator's full watch-list triage (buy now / wait for dip / wait for correction) across all ten names, including the actual 1911 Gold add. LeapEdge covers only four names, has the wrong ticker for New Pacific (NEWP), files the do-not-buy Banyan as a LONG, and calls a long-term accumulation plan 'swing'. Ours' weaknesses are real, though: every junior miner has a null ticker, which the omissions justify as a policy. SSR is mislabeled 'watch', stances contradict across duplicates, and the gold 4,000/4,125 levels were dropped out of over-caution.
recommendations: Group the output by the creator's own buckets. This video is a triage: 'Buy now: SSRM, NUAG, GGD, ARTG (+ added AUMB)'; 'Wait for shallow dip: BYN, CBR, NEXG'; 'Wait for correction: MUX, LUN'. A single structured 'action bucket' field would beat LeapEdge's 4 cards.

Resolve small-cap and TSX/TSXV miners with exchange suffixes. Remove the policy line 'Specific ticker symbols are omitted where not explicitly stated'; the PM needs BYN, CBR, NEXG, AUMB, NUAG, LUN, GGD, ARTG.
Promote names that appear only in tickerSentiment (GGD, Artemis) to calls when the creator says 'we're buying'.
Normalize ASR garbles before extraction ('250-day' -> '200/50-day'; '4,125 therapy session' -> gold $4,125) instead of dropping the number to omissions.
Enforce one stance per ticker per video, or an explicit time-ordered change. Banyan must not be neutral/avoid, bullish/watch and bullish/avoid at once.
Capture trade-activity facts ('bought 3 positions this week, 4th only 50% filled') and the gold reference levels (20% below ATH; 4,000 = -9.5%).
